html:
SMTO-GML-0032 — SMTO couldn't complete a request to Gmail

GUID: 8e6a58dd-5e9f-4eaf-b44d-e7b52dd8e90f
Slug: gmail-provider-error
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO asked Google to do something in Gmail, and Google, or the connection to Google, returned an error that SMTO couldn't narrow down further.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Gmail in a web browser and make sure it loads and you can sign in to the account the Task used. If Gmail or Google sign-in is down or blocked, SMTO can't reach it either.
  2. If the Task was sending or changing email, check Sent, Drafts or Trash in Gmail to see whether it already happened. This error doesn't show whether Google made the change before it failed.
  3. If the problem continues, ask SMTO to reconnect the same account, for example 'Connect Gmail using @gmail_auth_app and save the account as work_gmail', using your own names. A failed renewal of the account's Google sign-in shows up as this error, and reconnecting renews it.
  4. Then ask SMTO again in the conversation, only for what is still missing. Asking only for missing work avoids doing the same change twice.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the Gmail request and shows the results or the change in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete your Gmail account from Parameter Store or turn off security checks to make the error go away.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gmail API or Google OAuth request failed with a status or transport failure not covered by a more specific category, for example an unexpected 4xx response, a failed access-token refresh, or an unreachable OAuth endpoint.

What this means

  • Gmail/OAuth transport or provider processing raises a generic API error after more specific safe status categories do not apply. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • Gmail/OAuth transport or provider processing raises a generic API error after more specific safe status categories do not apply.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect safe provider status, transport stage and original write receipts without assuming a transient outage.

How to fix it

  • Read the recorded provider status and stage in Technical details and the GmailApiError in the Server log. Check Google service health and the Server's reachability of gmail.googleapis.com and oauth2.googleapis.com; for a token-refresh failure, reconnect the same account key through gmail.connect with the same Gmail OAuth App. For any write, inspect the live mailbox before resubmitting it.
  • Inspect the recorded provider status and service health; establish mailbox state before repeating mutations.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The actual request cause is addressed and prior mutation state is reconciled.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
